prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map captures the 3D layout of a cluttered indoor room as the camera wearer turns from facing a crib and storage bins (frames 1-2) toward a left wall and green shelf (frames 3-4), then looks down at two people seated below (frame 5). In frames 1 and 2, a bright silhouette in the lower-left foreground (about 0.3-0.5 m away, within arm's reach and partly cropped at the bottom edge) and a standing child in the lower-right/center foreground (about 1.0-1.2 m away, facing away toward a crib/laundry pile ~1.8-2.2 m behind them and a white bin on the right) stand out in front of a blue storage bin and black box on the far left (~2.5-3.0 m away). As the camera wearer rotates left in frames 3 and 4, the left wall becomes very bright (~0.4-0.8 m away, within arm's reach) while the shelving unit in the corner sits at medium depth (~1.2-1.8 m); in frame 5, looking downward reveals the green shelf on the upper left (~0.8-1.2 m away), a very bright head in the lower-left foreground (~0.4 m away, within arm's reach), a second seated person just behind and to the right (~1.0-1.2 m away, within reach of the first person), a round dark seat/table in the lower-right foreground (~0.8 m away), and the blue bin in the upper-right background (~2.5 m away). Compared to the motion-blurred RGB strip, the depth map clearly separates foreground heads and bodies from cluttered background furniture and walls, and shows the sharp depth discontinuity of the doorframe on the far right of frame 2. However, the depth map looks unreliable during heavy motion blur in frames 3 and 4, where the shelving unit and foreground figures merge into smooth, indistinct gradients, and it flattens fine geometry like the chair spindles and shelf supports.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map is extremely sparse across the 5 frames, detecting only a single 'person' mask in frame 1 and a single 'bed' mask in frame 2 while leaving frames 3, 4, and 5 completely blank. In frame 1, the pink 'person' mask outlines the child in the lower-right foreground (roughly 1.0-1.2 m from the camera wearer, facing away and right, with their lower body cropped by the bottom frame edge), and in frame 2, the teal 'bed' mask covers the cluttered crib/playpen in the left-center midground (roughly 1.5-2.2 m away, just behind and to the left of the child). Where present, these masks provide cleaner outer boundaries for the child's torso/head and the crib's overall extent than the motion-blurred RGB frames alone. However, the map is largely unreliable for scene understanding because it fails to segment the child in frame 2 (creating a false occlusion cutout in the bottom-right corner of the 'bed' mask where the child stands in front of it) and completely misses the close foreground person at the bottom-left of frames 1-2 (~0.3-0.5 m away). Furthermore, due to severe motion blur and downward viewing angles, it detects no objects or people at all in frames 3-5, missing the green shelf, the blue storage bin, the chairs, and the two close people (~0.4-1.2 m away, within arm's reach) at the bottom of frame 5.
descriptions.pose: The body and hand skeleton map is completely black across all 5 frames, failing to detect any body keypoints or hand skeletons in the entire sequence. From the RGB strip and depth map, several people are actually present at close to medium range: a person's head/shoulder at the bottom-left of frames 1-2 (~0.3-0.5 m away, within arm's reach), a child standing ~1.0-1.2 m in front of the camera wearer in frames 1-2 facing away toward the crib and white bin, and two people at the bottom-left and center of frame 5 (~0.4 m and ~1.0-1.2 m below and in front of the camera wearer, looking down/away rather than toward the camera, with a hand visible near the bottom center). None of these body orientations, gaze directions, or hand positions within arm's reach are captured by the pose map. Consequently, the pose map contributes no spatial information beyond the RGB strip and is completely unreliable here due to severe motion blur, strong downward egocentric viewing angles, and heavy truncation/occlusion of bodies at the bottom edges of the frames.
